text:
alex: Heads up — getting noisy-neighbor alerts for eu-west dedicated-slice-3. UI shows tail latency up x5 and several requests routed to 'fallback-small' model. Not sure why pool still has free GPU capacity.
priya: Can you paste the allocator logs and the router decisions? :eyes:
alex: quick excerpt from allocator around the time (simplified):
```
[6573219801] alloc-svc: slice=dedicated-slice-3 try-claim gpu=pm-12 status=ALLOC_FAIL reason=interlock-conflict
[6573219802] alloc-svc: fallback to shared-pool request_id=abc123 route=router-eu-west-2
[6573219803] router: chosen=fallthrough-small-model latency_est=120ms
```
morgan: That alloc-svc line looks like a MIG / vGPU interlock issue. we've seen pm-12 keep a stale carveout marker. Did anything touch the host? ops-bot: Recorded host reboot at 6573219700 by maintenance-window:eu-west-3.
sam: If host was rebooted, our carveout GC sometimes doesn't run if preemption watcher crashes. Can someone check allocctl: `allocctl check-interlock --host pm-12 --slice dedicated-slice-3`?
alex: ran it, output: `INTERLOCK: marker_present=true, marker_owner=dedicated-slice-7, last_heartbeat=6573205000` — owner mismatch.
jen: Hmm that explains overlap. dedicated-slice-7 should be on pm-13. Why did marker move? Could be a race during warm prefill where slice-7 transiently grabbed pm-12 then failed to release.
priya: routing side: router logs show it prefers keepalive lanes but will fall back after 250ms to small-model. That matches user-facing spike. We should avoid fallback for dedicated tenants until interlock resolved or they'll see reduced quality.
morgan: Proposed immediate mitigation: add quick reject on router for routes that match dedicated-slice IDs when alloc reports interlock_conflict, so we don't degrade to lower model, instead queue or 429 with informative error. Thoughts?
sam: +1 for a short-term guard. But 429 might break client expectations. Maybe respond with `503 degraded` and reason header `x-redwood-reason: interlock-conflict` so higher stacks can retry/backoff.
jen: Also schedule a GC run on pm-12 and audit carveout state across the rack. I'll kick an infra job: `infra-bot run carveout-gc --host pm-12 --force`.
ops-bot: A job was scheduled: job_id=gc-6573219999 started by jen.
alex: After GC, allocctl shows marker cleared. Re-ran a few requests and router picked dedicated model again, latency normalized. However we saw a second burst on a different host (pm-21) 10m later.
priya: Could this be a systemic prefill race under high allocation churn? We should correlate allocation churn rate with carveout marker churn.
morgan: Data team note: I'll pull churn metrics (alloc-create, alloc-destroy per host) for last 2h and correlate with interlock events.
sam: Long term: we need stronger lease semantics for carveouts (versioned tokens + lease renewal) instead of a boolean marker. Short term: add router guard + GC enforcement + alert dedupe so pagers don't flood.
alex: Agree. Can we also add a cost note — fallback to small model increases per-token cost for hosts hitting shared pools because of extra cache misses. Priya, can you estimate cost delta for last hour?
priya: Quick estimate: 40k tokens served on fallback at 3x cost => ~ +$0.12 for the hour for this slice. Not huge but visible across many tenants.
jen: I'll file an ops runbook update: carveout-GC checklist + router-guard flag + incident postmortem stub.
infra-bot: Incident stub created: /incidents/6573219876-alloc-interlock, assigned to eng-infra.
alex: Thanks everyone. Monitoring: keep an eye on egress routing changes and allocator interlock count. I'll update thread if anything else pops up. :thumbsup:
